title: What If Humans Could Photosynthesize?

scenes.text: What if humans could photosynthesize? Sunlight on your skin beats your diet, but it wouldn't feed you.
Eating about 2,000 calories a day equals roughly 100 watts of power, around the clock.
Noon sunlight brings about 1,000 watts per square meter, and you have roughly 2 square meters of skin.
Plants convert 1 to 2 percent of sunlight, so skin would make at best 20 to 40 watts at noon.
Night, shade, clothes and clouds cut that more. Over a day, you'd cover a small slice of your 100 watts.
One animal manages it: a sea slug steals chloroplasts from algae, then survives on photosynthesis for six to eight months.

description:
What if humans could photosynthesize?
Sunlight on your skin carries more energy than your food, but plants convert only 1 to 2 percent of it, so you would still need to eat.
What should we run through next?
